hook: SCP-3004 is split into tabbed documents, and it is built to be opened in the order they are listed. It deals seriously with Christianity, ritual and faith, and its ritual descriptions include the killing of a child, forced castration, and a stillbirth at an altar, so pick a moment when you are up for something heavy. Take the first tab at face value; that is part of how it works.
whyItMatters: Its central idea is that a god-like entity takes its shape and appetite from what people believe, and the horror flows from belief itself rather than from a monster in a cell. Christianity, Irish history and Foundation ethics are not background here but the actual material of the argument. Each tab has a different narrator, a scholar, a field agent and an ethics committee member, and each brings their own faith, or lack of it, to the same problem.
thingsToNotice:
The first tab is Father Clark's archived report: a cicada-worshipping Irish cult was wiped out in the 1700s, its god went quiet, and the file is marked Neutralized. The second tab flips that to Keter, because the entity has latched onto Catholic and Anglican congregations, and the listed rituals are deliberately unsparing: a priest biting out the throat of a child bearing stigmata, children tearing out a priest's teeth to serve as communion, every male past puberty castrated, a woman giving birth on the altar to dozens of wood-and-glass cicadas and a dead infant in a wooden crown.

Agent Luttermann's astral-projection report is casual and shaken; he finds the entity alone in nothingness, half-awake, convinced it is God and that it is handing people back their cicadas as a gift, and it swallows him like a communion wafer and feeds on his memories of Mass. The last tab is Bridget Callaghan's ethics vote for Protocol Damnatio ad Bestias, which erases Christianity from history by feeding a willing Catholic reality bender, "St. Jude the Damned," to twelve machines called the Lions forever. She frames it as an eternal suffering undoing Christ's sacrifice and signs off unsure whether she is damning herself along with him.

related.note: The addendum notes it stopped appearing once these events began and suspects a link.
